goal: Expose one read-only operational view across DC-Agent task sources while keeping Codex an optional advanced executor instead of runtime authority.

acceptance_criteria.description: The Task Control Plane normalizes launchd, crontab, Codex automation, watchdog probe, Knowledge Cycle, AstrBot Cron, and Harness task records into one stable task shape.
Codex-backed records are explicitly classified as advanced_executor and never as deterministic_controller.
A paused Feishu knowledge workflow is reported as paused even when its last worker exit code was successful.
watchdogctl JSON status preserves legacy sections and adds the unified control_plane snapshot without mutating runtime state.
Knowledge Cycle records a paused Feishu workflow without spawning its worker until the operator removes the pause marker.
The legacy AstrBot HTTP restart cron is marked superseded by launchd lifecycle ownership and the unified watchdog probes.
watchdogctl can retire only an explicitly superseded scheduler entry while preserving every unrelated crontab line.
Group and single-task resume operations never reactivate superseded schedulers or Codex automation heartbeats.
The legacy Feishu launchd scheduler is superseded by the paused Knowledge Cycle Feishu/NAS workflow and cannot be restored by group resume.
Knowledge Cycle never automatically schedules the legacy Feishu repair step, while the shared feishu_sync Implementation remains available to the authoritative targeted workflow.
Group resume first returns an Activation Plan containing only inactive authoritative tasks; superseded tasks and Codex automations never enter the plan.
Group resume executes only when the caller confirms the exact current plan_id, and rejects missing or stale confirmations without mutating runtime state.
Group pause first returns a Deactivation Plan containing only active controllable tasks, while the authoritative dc-watchdog remains protected from group operations.
Pause and resume share one Control Plan Interface and both reject missing, expired, stale, or wrong-operation confirmations without runtime mutations.
Critical single-task pauses expose their operational impact and require an item-scoped Control Plan bound to the exact scheduler kind, key, operation, state, and execution identity.
A missing, expired, stale, group-scoped, wrong-operation, or wrong-target plan cannot authorize a critical single-task pause or mutate runtime state.
watchdog repair budgets, recent outcomes, and circuit-breaker state are projected into the read-only control plane and Dashboard without adding repair execution controls.
Manual repair reviews are visible in the control plane, while acknowledgement and resolution use item-scoped Control Plans that never execute runtime repair commands.
